query: For the paper "Sequential Neural Networks as Automata" (arXiv: 1906.01615), answer this question: How do attention, recurrent and convolutional networks differ on the language classes they accept?

drafts: The passages do not specify the language class accepted by attention networks. They state only that attention is among the architectures for which automata-theoretic characterizations are derived [2], and that the paper characterizes languages acceptable by recurrent networks, attention, and convolutional networks [3]. For the architectures that are characterized: LSTMs function like counter machines, and convolutional networks are related to the subregular hierarchy [3]; additionally, LSTMs are connected to counter automata, with a construction by which an LSTM can simulate a simplified variant of a counter automaton [22]. The specific language class for attention is not given in these passages, so that part of the comparison cannot be established from the provided evidence.
循环网络（LSTM）被刻画为类似计数器机器 [3]，并有构造使 LSTM 能模拟简化版计数器自动机 [22]；卷积网络被联系到子正则层级 [3]。至于注意力网络具体接受哪一类语言，所提供的段落未给出其语言类刻画，因而注意力与这两类网络在接受语言类上的具体差异无法从这些证据中确定。

citations.quote: We use this theory to derive computation upper bounds and automata-theoretic characterizations for sev- eral different kinds of recurrent neural networks (Section 3), as well as other architectural vari- ants like attention (Section 4) and convolutional networks (CNNs) (Section 5).

We then characterize the classes of languages acceptable by various recurrent net- works, attention, and convolutional networks. We ﬁnd that LSTMs function like counter ma- chines and relate convolutional networks to the subregular hierarchy.

Weiss et al. (2018) propose a connection between long short- term memory networks (LSTMs) and counter au- tomata. They provide a construction by which the LSTM can simulate a simpliﬁed variant of a counter automaton.

cited_sources.text: (2018) by an- alyzing the expressiveness of neural network ac- ceptors under asymptotic conditions. We formal- ize asymptotic language acceptance, as well as an associated notion of network memory. We use this theory to derive computation upper bounds and automata-theoretic characterizations for sev- eral different kinds of recurrent neural networks (Section 3), as well as other architectural vari- ants like attention (Section 4) and convolutional networks (CNNs) (Section 5).

We then characterize the classes of languages acceptable by various recurrent net- works, attention, and convolutional networks. We ﬁnd that LSTMs function like counter ma- chines and relate convolutional networks to the subregular hierarchy.

Weiss et al. (2018) propose a connection between long short- term memory networks (LSTMs) and counter au- tomata. They provide a construction by which the LSTM can simulate a simpliﬁed variant of a counter automaton. They also demonstrate that LSTMs can learn to increment and decrement their cell state as counters in practice.
